title: Mirabai Chanu, Manu Bhaker Lead India's Medal Hunt on Asian Games Day 5
excerpt: Olympic medallists Mirabai Chanu and Manu Bhaker headline a packed Day 5 in Aichi-Nagoya, with at least eight medal events on Wednesday's schedule.
body:
• Olympic medallists Mirabai Chanu and Manu Bhaker headline India's busiest medal day yet at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games on Wednesday, September 23.
  • Chanu contests the women's 49kg weightlifting final at 10:00 AM IST, chasing the one major medal missing from her cabinet — and India's first Asian Games weightlifting medal since 1998.
  • Bhaker leads India's trio in the women's 10m air pistol final at 9:00 AM, with skeet shooters also in medal contention through the morning.
  • The men's badminton team faces China in the semifinal at 11:30 AM, already assured of a medal after beating Japan in the quarterfinals.

India's campaign at the 2026 Asian Games gathers pace on Wednesday, with two of the country's biggest sporting names — Olympic medallists Mirabai Chanu and Manu Bhaker — headlining a packed Day 5 schedule in Aichi-Nagoya. The women's cricket team opened India's gold-medal account on Tuesday with a commanding win over Sri Lanka in the final, and the contingent heads into Wednesday with eight medals in the bag — one gold, four silver and three bronze — and at least eight more medal events on the slate.

Chanu chases the missing medal

The day's most anticipated moment arrives at 10:00 AM IST, when Mirabai Chanu takes the platform in the women's 49kg weightlifting final. The Tokyo 2020 silver medallist is pursuing the one major multi-sport medal that has eluded her: she finished fourth at Hangzhou 2023 after an injury forced her to withdraw from her final clean-and-jerk attempt.

The stakes go beyond personal history. India has not won an Asian Games weightlifting medal since Karnam Malleswari's silver in 1998 — a 28-year drought that Chanu, arriving in form after gold at the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow earlier this year, is expected to end. Gyaneshwari Yadav follows in the women's 53kg final at 1:30 PM, giving India a second shot at the podium in the afternoon.

Bhaker begins her shooting campaign

The first medal window opens early. Manu Bhaker, Esha Singh and Suruchi Inder Singh shoot the women's 10m air pistol qualification at 6:15 AM IST, with the individual final scheduled for 9:00 AM. Bhaker, a double Olympic medallist from Paris 2024, missed out on an individual medal at Hangzhou and will be looking to correct that record on the continental stage.

Shooting offers more chances through the morning. The skeet competitions conclude their three-day programme, with Maheshwari Chauhan, Parinaaz Dhaliwal and Razia Dhillon in the women's individual final at 11:00 AM, and Anantjeet Singh Naruka, Mairaj Khan and Bhavtegh Singh Gill carrying India's hopes in the men's event after a strong second day of qualification.

Team sports take centre stage

The men's badminton team faces its sternest test yet — a semifinal against China at 11:30 AM. Lakshya Sen and his teammates secured at least a bronze by beating Japan in the quarterfinals; a win over the tournament favourites would put India in the gold-medal match and set up one of the stories of the Games.

At the same hour, the women's hockey team plays Thailand in Pool B, while both kabaddi teams are in group action — the women face Iran at 8:30 AM and the men meet Bangladesh at 9:45 AM. In wushu, Roshibina Devi contests the women's 60kg sanda semifinal against Indonesia's Thania Kusumaningtyas at 2:30 PM, another realistic medal opportunity.

What to watch from dawn

India's day begins as early as 5:30 AM IST, with Jay Meena's men's singles soft tennis quarterfinal against the Philippines' Sherwin Nuguit and the men's sepaktakraw team facing the Philippines. Meena could play three times in the day if he keeps winning, with a semifinal at 8:30 AM and the gold-medal match at 12:15 PM. Rowing, canoe sprint, fencing and table tennis fill out the morning programme, while equestrian riders Fouaad Mirza, Arjan Singh Nagra and Ashish Limaye contest the eventing cross-country medal round.

Thursday brings no let-up: the men's 10m air pistol final and the mixed skeet team final are among the next medal chances. But Wednesday, with Chanu and Bhaker both in action, is the day India's medal tally is expected to move most.
